articleTitle: A Golay sequencer based NDT system for highly attenuating materials
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Non-Contacting and Remote NDT
abstract: In conventional pulse transmission based ultrasonic measurement systems the signal to noise ratio is constrained by the maximum permissible pulse amplitude which may be applied to the transmitter and the thermal noise generated by the receiver amplifier. By exciting the transmitting transducer with a wideband noise source and performing the cross correlation between the exciting noise source and the receiver output an improvement in signal to noise ratio of 40 dB is possible.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Through transmission ultrasonic NDT without coupling fluids
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Non-Contacting and Remote NDT
abstract: The difficulties associated with through transmission airborne NDT are discussed using an acoustic simulation model. The model, based on a combination of finite element and linear systems theory, is used to optimise a separate transmit-receive transducer arrangement operating under high energy, narrowband conditions. A series of composite transducers are then evaluated theoretically and tested for airborne operation at frequencies between 250 kHz and 1.5 MHz, using excitation voltages down to 50 V. Through transmission airborne signatures are demonstrated on a number of solid samples, including glass, aluminium and carbon-fibre composite plates ranging from 3-50 mm in thickness.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Remote NDT for the aerospace industry
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Non-Contacting and Remote NDT
abstract: The various advantages offered by non-contacting NDT methods are briefly reviewed. Particular attention is given to the questions of improving the speed and convenience of inspection and of compatibility with automation. The NDT techniques in current use are considered where the limitations of current techniques are contrasted with the potential of the non-contacting methods under development.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Recent progress using SQUIDS for non-contact NDE
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Non-Contacting and Remote NDT
abstract: SQUIDs have a promising future for non-contact NDE. Initial impracticality due to poor spatial resolution has been overcome and SQUIDs have been demonstrated detecting real defects. While present systems have attractive capabilities they are expensive to buy and operate, and far too cumbersome for wide application. However, it seems certain that similar performance will be provided by HTS systems within a few years, without the cost and impracticality with which present users have to contend.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Mathematical modelling of 1-3 connectivity composite transducers for through air NDT applications
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Non-Contacting and Remote NDT
abstract: The authors outline a mathematical modelling strategy (using FEM) for behavioural prediction of 1-3 connectivity composite piezoelectric transducers in air coupled and other applications. A dual strategy is employed embracing the microstructure of the composite device, followed by simulation of the macro system characteristics.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Non-contact ultrasound using pulsed laser generation
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Non-Contacting and Remote NDT
abstract: Pulsed lasers have been used for many applications in the field of non-contact and remote NDT. The authors describe some recent advances in the use of this source in combination with several types of non-contact detector, to result in a truly remote ultrasonic testing system with a range of applications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
